Subject: Slate Labs pilot: throughput targets & budget bridge (post-call)

Hi Rachel — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a tight pilot pricing proposal.

What I captured from the call:
- Primary objective: pilot Redwood Dedicated to serve Slate Labs' real-time summarization feature for customer support.
- Expected steady-state: 1.0–1.8M tokens/day (average), with short peaks up to ~12 requests/sec during US business hours.
- Latency target: 150–250ms p95 for 512-token responses (lower latency preferred).
- Initial pilot length: 30 days, scaling to production commit if throughput and cost align.

Questions / asks for the proposal:
1) Budget guardrail: you mentioned a target of ~$20/1M tokens as a ballpark. Can you confirm a firm range (e.g., $15–25/1M) for procurement to evaluate?
2) GPU preference: is there an internal leaning toward H100 (latency advantage) or A100/80GB (cost advantage)? If no preference, we’ll show two priced options.
3) Commit sizing: would you be comfortable with a small reserved lane (equivalent to 2 reserved GPUs for the pilot) or prefer burstable dedicated capacity? Pilot economics change materially either way.
4) Compliance / procurement: please share the procurement contact and any SOC2, DPA or IP terms we should include in the proposal.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll draft a one-page pilot pricing bridge with two GPU options + throughput mapping and a per-1M token unit price.
- Camila will attach a throughput matrix mapping requests/sec and avg tokens to GPU lanes so you can see headroom.
- If procurement is ready, we’ll route a formal quote to procurement and timeline the pilot start (target next week).

Attachments I will include in the draft: pricing proposal PDF + throughput_matrix XLSX (pilot sizing).

Would appreciate confirmation on the budget range and procurement contact; I’ll aim to send a formal pilot quote by EOD tomorrow PST.

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan — quick clarifications below.

On volumes: our product analytics team estimates 1.5M tokens/day average during pilot, with heavier spikes around new feature rollouts that could push bursts to ~14 req/sec for short windows. The 1.0–1.8M band you have is reasonable.

Budget: $20/1M tokens is our internal target; procurement will accept 15–25/1M for evaluation but prefers anything at or below $20 if the latency numbers hold.

GPU choice: we care about latency more than absolute cost — H100 would be preferred if the delta is <2x compared to A100, otherwise we need the cost-per-1M token to stay near that $20 target. Please include both options.

Compliance: we do require SOC 2 Type II evidence and standard DPA language. Procurement is cc’d here — Ben from procurement will take the formal quote.

Also: we’d like a simple mapping of 'requests/sec at X avg tokens' to reserved GPU lanes and expected p95 latency so engineering can plan.

Thanks — Rachel

Hi all — quick technical mapping and two concrete capacity options for the pilot. Attaching a small XLSX that maps requests/sec (RPS) and avg token payload to GPU-lane equivalents; summary below.

Assumptions (pilot model): avg output 512 tokens, model is a 13B sparse-quantized variant (production model TBD).

Option A — Cost-optimized (A100 80GB lanes):
- Reserved lanes: 2x A100 80GB
- Expected sustained throughput: ~8–10 RPS at 512 tokens (headroom for bursts to ~14 RPS with queuing / short-term burst lanes).
- Expected p95 latency: ~220–320ms (depends on batching and KV cache warm).
- Unit economics: we'll price this at $~15–18/1M tokens (pilot ramp discount applied).

Option B — Latency-priority (H100 80GB lanes):
- Reserved lanes: 2x H100 80GB
- Expected sustained throughput: ~12–14 RPS at 512 tokens (comfortable headroom for the bursts you described).
- Expected p95 latency: ~120–200ms.
- Unit economics: ~ $28–32/1M tokens (H100 infra + higher perf fraction).

Notes:
- Quantization + continuous KV caching for prefixes will reduce per-token GPU work ~12–18% across both configs; we can show a "reduced cost" column in the XLSX.
- If you want to hit $20/1M tokens and keep H100 latency, consider a mixed lane: 1x H100 + 1x A100 (gives ~200ms p95 with ~ $20–23/1M projected).

I’ve attached throughput_matrix_SL-4021.xlsx with the RPS -> lane mapping and a simple cost calc. Let me know if you want me to run a short microbenchmark against your sample prompt set (we can do that in a day with a small prompt corpus).

-Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
